newsitem.title: USA: Trial begins for Berrigan, other peace protesters.
newsitem.headline: Trial begins for Berrigan, other peace protesters.

text.p: A federal trial began Monday for veteran peace activist Phillip Berrigan and five others charged with vandalising a warship to protest nuclear weapons.
About 100 people demonstrated outside the courthouse in support of the activists, who could get up to 15 years in prison if convicted on charges of destruction of government property and conspiracy.

The members of the "Prince of Peace Ploughshares" allegedly smashed controls and spilled blood Feb. 26 on the bridge of the destroyer USS The Sullivans, which was under construction at Bath Iron Works.
According to court documents, the group gained access to the ship by telling guards they were from General Dynamics Corp, owner of the Bath, Maine, shipyard to test security.
Officials claim the incident caused $80,000 damage.

The defendents Monday claimed they did not intend to act illegally because they were following international laws aimed at stopping the spread of nuclear weapons. The Sullivans is capable of carrying nuclear warheads.

U.S. District Court Judge Gene Carter took under advisement a prosecution motion to dismiss the group's evidence about the danger of nuclear war. Carter allowed some of the evidence to be aired without the jury in the room.

Berrigan, 73, a former Roman Catholic priest, has been active in the peace movement since the Vietnam War era. He was arrested in the Bath shipyard in 1991, but a state court later dropped the trespass charge.
The courthouse protesters, who had come to Maine from around the Northeast, sang traditional antiwar songs and carried signs that read "Peacemakers on Trial" and "Warpower to Peacepower."
"I'm just amazed at the turnout of marvellous people. It's like old home week," said Daniel Berrigan, Phillip's brother, who has also long been active in the peace movement.

Phillip Berrigan and the other defendents Stephen Kelley, 48, of New York, Susan Crane, 53, of Ukiah, California, Thomas Borbely, 56, of Worcester, Massachusetts, Steven Baggarly, 31, of Norfolk, Virginia and Mark Colville, 36, of New Haven, Connecticut, are acting as their own attorneys.
The group has been confined to the Cumberland County Jail since their arrest because they refused to abide by bail conditions that required them to stay away from Bath Iron Works' property.
